zoning_density.t: Cities should be required to allow apartment buildings in most neighborhoods.
yes: Ending single-family-only zoning in high-cost cities and suburbs
Apartment buildings on most residential streets
no: Keeping neighborhoods limited to single houses

zoning_density.t: Allow duplexes and townhomes in single-family neighborhoods, but not large apartment buildings.
yes: Two- to four-unit homes and townhomes on single-family lots
no: Large apartment buildings in those neighborhoods

zoning_density.t: Each neighborhood should decide what can be built.
yes: Neighborhood votes or local boards deciding on new housing types
no: City or state rules requiring more housing types

yes: Neighborhoods limited to one house per lot
no: Duplexes, townhomes or apartments in those neighborhoods

zoning_state_override.t: States should override local zoning whenever cities fall short of housing goals.
yes: State laws forcing cities to allow more homes when they miss targets

zoning_state_override.t: States should override local zoning only near transit and job centers.
yes: State-required apartments near train stations and job hubs
Cities and towns setting their own zoning

housing_approval.t: Housing that meets every rule should be approved automatically.
yes: By-right approval with no hearings
Ending lawsuits that delay rule-following projects
no: Public hearings for projects that already follow the rules

housing_approval.t: Approve rule-following housing after a short public comment period.
yes: A brief comment period, then approval

housing_approval.t: Neighbors should have a say through hearings and the right to sue.
yes: Public hearings and lawsuits over new housing, even if it meets the rules

rent_control.t: Cities should strictly limit rent increases, such as to inflation.
yes: Capping yearly rent increases for existing tenants at inflation

rent_control.t: Moderate limits on rent increases, with new buildings exempt.
yes: Caps of about inflation plus a few percent
Exempting newly built housing

rent_control.t: Limit rent increases only temporarily during emergencies.
yes: Emergency caps after disasters
Letting landlords set rents freely
State bans on local rent control

eviction_cause.t: Landlords should need a specific reason to evict or not renew any tenant.
yes: Just-cause eviction rules for all tenants
no: Ending a lease just because its term is up

eviction_cause.t: Landlords should need a reason only for tenants who've lived there a year or more.
yes: Just-cause protection after a year

eviction_cause.t: Landlords can end a lease when its term ends.
yes: Non-renewal without giving a reason

rent_vouchers.t: Every eligible low-income family should get federal rent help.
yes: Funding vouchers for all eligible households, up from about 1 in 4

rent_vouchers.t: Help more families with rent vouchers than today.
yes: Expanding voucher funding

rent_vouchers.t: Keep rent help at about today's level.
yes: Today's voucher funding

rent_vouchers.t: Help fewer families with rent; rely more on the private market.
yes: Cutting federal rental help

public_housing.t: Government should build and own a large amount of housing for people of all incomes.
yes: Large-scale public housing open to all incomes, like Vienna's

public_housing.t: Government should build and own housing for low-income people.
yes: More public housing for low-income families
no: Leaving it all to the market

public_housing.t: Government should pay private builders through tax credits instead of owning housing.
yes: Tax credits for private affordable housing
No government building or subsidizing of housing

encampments.t: Allow people to camp in public until there's enough shelter or housing.
yes: Letting people stay on sidewalks and in parks when they have nowhere else
no: Clearing camps without a place to go

encampments.t: Clear camps only after offering each person a shelter bed.
yes: Clearing camps once a bed is offered
no: Letting camps stay when beds are available

encampments.t: Ban camping and clear camps, even without enough shelter beds.
yes: Clearing camps whether or not shelter is available
no: Letting people camp on sidewalks or in parks

encampments.t: Ban camping, with fines or jail for people who don't move.
yes: Fines or jail for refusing to leave a camp

housing_first.t: House homeless people first, with no requirement to be sober or in treatment.
yes: Giving housing without conditions on drug use or treatment

housing_first.t: House people first, but require treatment to keep the housing.
yes: Housing tied to staying in treatment

housing_first.t: Treatment or sobriety should come first, before housing.
yes: Making sobriety or treatment a condition for getting housing

involuntary_treatment.t: Keep treatment voluntary except when someone is an immediate danger.
yes: Today's immediate-danger standard
no: Committing people who can't meet basic needs

involuntary_treatment.t: Also require treatment when people can't meet basic needs like food and shelter.
yes: Widening involuntary treatment to people who can't care for themselves

involuntary_treatment.t: Make it much easier to require treatment, including longer hospital stays.
yes: Broader involuntary commitment
Longer required hospital stays

investor_homes.t: Ban large investment firms from buying single-family homes to rent out.
yes: Barring firms with hundreds of homes from buying more

investor_homes.t: Allow large investors to buy homes, but with limits or extra taxes.
yes: Caps or extra taxes on large investors' home purchases

investor_homes.t: Let large investment firms buy homes to rent; they add rental housing.
yes: No limits on investor purchases
no: Bans or extra taxes on investors

short_term_rentals.t: Ban short-term rentals like Airbnb in most neighborhoods.
yes: Banning whole-home nightly rentals in residential areas

short_term_rentals.t: Allow short-term rentals only in the owner's own home.
yes: Renting your own home or a room in it
Banning investor-owned nightly rentals
no: Allowing any whole home to be rented nightly

short_term_rentals.t: Allow short-term rentals with registration and taxes.
yes: Registration and hotel-style taxes for short-term rentals
Letting owners rent their homes by the night freely

mortgage_deduction.t: End the mortgage interest deduction and use the money for renters or first-time buyers.
yes: Repealing the deduction
Aid for renters or first-time buyers

mortgage_deduction.t: Keep the mortgage interest deduction only for smaller mortgages.
yes: Lowering the cap on mortgages that qualify

mortgage_deduction.t: Keep the mortgage interest deduction as it is.
yes: Today's deduction

mortgage_deduction.t: Expand the mortgage interest deduction to help more homeowners.
yes: Letting homeowners who don't itemize claim it
A higher cap

transit_vs_roads.t: Shift much more transportation money to transit and away from new roads.
yes: Large increases for buses, subways and trains
Fewer new highways and lanes

transit_vs_roads.t: Shift somewhat more transportation money to transit.
yes: Modest increases for buses and trains

transit_vs_roads.t: Keep about today's split between transit and roads.
yes: Today's transportation budgets

transit_vs_roads.t: Put more transportation money into roads and highways.
yes: More highways, lanes and bridges
Less for transit
